title: Bunny Ears Podcast #24 — David Choe
summary: A post-recording preface preserves the original Anthony Bourdain discussion after his death and adds the program's historical suicide-prevention message; current 988 guidance belongs outside, not inside, the literal transcript. A second preface explains Macaulay Culkin's pain during recording before Matt Cohen, Culkin and David Choe discuss privacy, child fame, financial independence, art, fandom and purpose. The episode itself says Culkin and Cohen sound difficult to distinguish in audio, strong evidence against adjacency-based speaker labels. Choe repeatedly admits projecting his own fears onto Culkin, child stars and guests. Culkin describes the podcast as controlled disclosure. Dense art stories cover Culkin's Korn painting, John Cusack, Nobu, Paul Hipp, a reported Culkin Christ garage work, possible Malibu tagging, Banksy-style object rights, an alleged $20,000 price-manufacturing scheme and Choe's incorrect stock-to-painting valuation, which Culkin directly challenges. The strongest creative sections ask why anyone works after money is unnecessary, defend play before monetization, seek childhood honesty, and map comics, toys, wrestling and fictional heroes as influence. Choe connects childhood alienation with villains and Korean Batman, then reaches David Chang, Bill Simmons, André the Giant, Samuel Beckett and a pre-death Bourdain dinner story. Dangerous steroid and gambling talk, private women and children, residences, property, restaurant routes and guest consent remain restricted rather than deleted. The closing production/voicemail material is separate from the guest conversation. Zero publisher speaker prefixes exist, so named line-level turns remain withheld.

speaker_policy.reason: The program establishes Macaulay Culkin, Matt Cohen and David Choe at episode level, plus prefaces, callers and production bits. But all 1,728 caption segments lack publisher speaker prefixes, and the conversation explicitly says Culkin and Cohen sound difficult to distinguish in podcast audio. The source also includes quotation, retrospective paraphrase, music, jokes, listener voicemails, scripted office dialogue and closing credits. Grammar, topic ownership, visual familiarity and adjacency cannot prove every line. Named turns require independently held-out, non-overlapping acoustic/video validation.
